title: A busy morning at WKU
paragraphs: It is Tuesday, the fourteenth of October. The time is 9:15 in the morning. My name is Amir Bekzhanov. I am nineteen years old and I am from Aktau. I study Computer Science at WKU. Right now, I am sitting in the WKU library on the second floor. I am not attending a lecture at this moment because my first class starts at eleven. I am using this free time to review my notes from yesterday. The library is not quiet this morning — it is full of students!

All around me, students are working hard. At the table next to mine, two girls are discussing something in low voices — I think they are preparing for a presentation. Near the window, a tall boy is sleeping with his head on his notebook. He is definitely not studying! One student near the entrance is talking on the phone — which is not allowed in the library. The librarian is already walking towards him with a stern look. In the corner, the printer is making a loud noise. Someone is printing a very long document.

I look out of the window. Down in the WKU courtyard, I can see many students. A group of friends is sitting on the steps near the main building, laughing and eating something — probably baursaks from the cafeteria. Two students are cycling across the courtyard towards the sports centre. A professor is walking quickly towards the main entrance. She is carrying a big pile of papers under her arm. She is probably going to give a lecture right now.

I decide to take a short break and go downstairs to the cafeteria. It is very busy. The cook is preparing fresh soup — the whole room is smelling of something warm and delicious. Students are standing in a long queue. The girl at the front of the queue is paying for her breakfast. The cashier is not smiling today — she looks very tired. My friend Bekzat is sitting at a corner table. He is eating a bowl of porridge and reading a textbook at the same time. That is very typical of Bekzat.

I take a coffee and go back upstairs. I pass the main lecture hall on the first floor. Through the glass in the door, I can see that a lecture is already starting. The professor is writing something on the whiteboard. About forty students are sitting in rows and taking notes. A few students near the back are looking at their phones, but the professor is not noticing them right now. I am happy I am not in that class today!

Back in the library, I open my laptop and start working. I am writing a program for my Computer Science project. It is quite difficult, but I am enjoying the challenge. Next to me, Malika Seitkali — a student from my dormitory floor — is reading a very thick book about Psychology. She is carefully highlighting sentences with a yellow marker. She does not usually study here — she normally works in her room — but today she is in the library because her internet is not working.

Suddenly, my phone buzzes. It is my mother calling from Aktau! I quickly go out into the corridor and answer. "Amir! What are you doing?" she asks. "I am studying, Mama," I reply. "Are you eating properly?" "Yes, Mama — I am eating very well!" She tells me that my father is fixing the car in the garage and my little sister Dinara is playing in the garden with the neighbour's dog. I miss them all. We talk for a few minutes, and then I go back to work.

I love mornings like this at WKU. Everyone is busy. Everyone is moving, thinking, reading, and learning. Right now, at this very moment, hundreds of students on this campus are working towards their future. I am one of them. At 10:45 I close my laptop and pick up my bag. My lecture is starting in fifteen minutes. I am ready.

dialogue.speaker: Amir

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.text: No — his lecture isn't starting for another hour. Let him sleep!
